title: OFFSET vs keyset pagination
claim: OFFSET gets slower the deeper you page, because skipped rows are still read. Keyset pagination
("rows after the last one seen") is equally fast on page 1 and page 1000.
verdict: Confirmed exactly. OFFSET grows with depth: page 1 {t:offset_page_1}, page 1,000 {t:offset_page_1000}, page
50,000 {t:offset_page_50000} (1M index entries read and discarded). Keyset stays at {t:keyset_page_50000} at any
depth, {x:offset_page_50000/keyset_page_50000} faster at page 50,000. OBP's /management/metrics pages with
offset/limit, so deep pages get slow.

sections.label: setup
sections.sql:
SET maintenance_work_mem = '1GB';
CREATE INDEX sc_metric_date_id ON metric (date_c DESC, id DESC);

sections.plan_text:
Limit | rows=20 (est 20) loops=1 time=0.015 ms | buffers hit=4 read=0
  -> Index Scan (sc_metric_date_id) | rows=20 (est 5032517) loops=1 time=0.013 ms | buffers hit=4 read=0

sections.desc: page 1 of all metrics, 20 per page
sections.sql: SELECT id, date_c, url, duration FROM metric ORDER BY date_c DESC, id DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 0;

sections.sql: SELECT id, date_c, url, duration FROM metric ORDER BY date_c DESC, id DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 19980;

sections.sql: SELECT id, date_c, url, duration FROM metric ORDER BY date_c DESC, id DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 999980;

sections.label: keyset_page_1000
sections.desc: page 1,000 via WHERE (date_c, id) < last row of page 999
sections.sql:
SELECT date_c AS last_date, id AS last_id FROM metric ORDER BY date_c DESC, id DESC OFFSET 19979 LIMIT 1 \gset
-- @explain
SELECT id, date_c, url, duration FROM metric
 WHERE (date_c, id) < (:'last_date', :last_id) ORDER BY date_c DESC, id DESC LIMIT 20;
